filter.notes: Find 'special' via memmem, then find 'requests' in remainder. Exclude matches.

scan.action: increment per-thread c_count array at o_custkey position for passing rows

join_order.notes: LEFT JOIN simulated via direct count array: c_count[custkey]++. All customers start at 0 (LEFT JOIN semantics). No explicit join needed — scan orders and accumulate counts by o_custkey.

data_structures.notes: Per-thread local arrays (6MB each × 64 = 384MB) avoid atomic contention. Merge after scan. max_c_count ≈ 40 so histogram is tiny.

details.method: scan merged c_count array, custdist[c_count]++ for all 1,500,000 customer keys

phases.scan_orders: parallel — partition 15M rows into morsels, each thread has local c_count array
phases.merge_counts: parallel — divide 1.5M custkey range across threads, sum per-thread arrays
phases.build_histogram: single_thread — only ~1.5M entries into ~40 buckets, trivially fast

mmap_strategy.raii_scoping: declare MMap objects at outer scope before RAII timer to exclude munmap TLB shootdown cost

critical_notes: Do NOT use MAP_POPULATE — demand-paged mmap with MADV_SEQUENTIAL for sequential scan
Per-thread local c_count arrays to avoid atomic contention on hot custkey slots
Customer keys range 1..1500000 contiguously — direct array is optimal (only 6MB each)
LEFT JOIN semantics: customers with no qualifying orders have c_count=0, must be counted in histogram
String matching: two-phase memmem — find 'special' (7 bytes), then 'requests' (8 bytes) in remainder
RAII timer scoping: munmap outside timing scope to avoid TLB shootdown cost
